sections.title: A time or a place becomes an adjective
sections.content: Add *-i* to a word for a time or a place and you get an adjective meaning "of that time" or "from that place": *ma* ("today") becomes *mai* ("today's"), *Budapest* becomes *budapesti* ("of Budapest"). The adjective goes before the noun, like every adjective you know. The ending is always *-i*: it never changes for vowel harmony, and place adjectives are written with a small letter, so *budapesti*, not *Budapesti*.

sections.title: Time words and place words with -i

items.english: The evening meeting is at seven.

sections.content: Compare the plain word with the adjective: *Ma van a találkozó* ("The meeting is today") but *a mai találkozó* ("today's meeting"). A few words bend a little: *este* drops its *-e* (*esti*, not *estei*), and *falu* ("village") becomes *falusi*, which you can simply learn as it comes. *reggeli* is also the noun "breakfast" you already know.
